I will keep my land in the usual wheat-maize rotation. In Quzhou County, this is the most reliable way for me to make use of the full year, and I trust it because I know how to manage it and it fits our water and field conditions. I will carry my winter wheat through to harvest, then I will seed summer maize right after wheat comes off so I do not lose moisture or time. I will not split land into too many crops, because at my age I want steady output and simpler field work, not extra risk. For wheat, I will use an improved variety, give it moderate fertilizer, irrigate at the key stages, and control weeds and disease a couple of times. After harvest, I will put in hybrid maize on the same land, mostly with no-tillage after wheat, push nitrogen a bit harder, water when needed, and spray only as much as necessary for weeds and insects. My goal is stable grain yield, manageable labor, and lower risk.
